newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA OUTPLAY S. AFRICA TO WIN BY 74 RUNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA OUTPLAY S. AFRICA TO WIN BY 74 RUNS.

text.p: Accurate bowling and superb fielding helped India bowl South Africa out for 193 runs to score an emphatic 74-run victory in the one-off one-day international match on Saturday.

Facing an uphill task of scoring 5.36 runs an over to win, the South Africans stumbled right at the start, losing opener Gary Kirsten for just one run with the total on four. He edged a ball from Venkatesh Prasad to Mohammed Azharuddin at slip.
South Africa never recovered, losing wickets at regular intervals to an accurate Indian attack, spearheaded by Prasad who ended up with an impressive 4-27 off eight overs.
South African skipper Hansie Cronje, playing his 100th one-day international and his 50th as captain, threw his wicket away just as the visitors looked like settling down from their early loss.
Cronje went for a wild slog on the legside but only managed to give a simple catch to Robin Singh at cover.

Andrew Hudson and Daryll Cullinan then got together for South Africa's best partnership of the match, 45 runs off 11.5 overs, before it was broken. Hudson was bowled round his legs trying to sweep left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi. He scored 45 runs in 61 balls with six hits to the boundary.
Cullinan with 45 and Herschelle Gibbs with 31 tried to lead a fightback but the task proved beyond them, the run rate rising to 6.52 by the 25th over.
The South Africans lost their last six wickets for just 66 runs as their batsmen fell against a steady Indian attack, trying desperately to lift the run-rate.
The Indians, who batted first after their skipper Sachin Tendulkar won the toss, scored 267 runs for six wickets.
A powerful century by Tendulkar, his 10th in one-day cricket, and a late burst by Ajay Jadeja helped India post a winning total.

In an eventful first session, marked by a protest walkout by the South Africans against unruly crowd behaviour, Tendulkar rode his luck after Gibbs dropped him at point off Brian Mcmillan when he was on three.
He went on to score 114 off 126 balls, a knock studded with 14 boundaries, before he was stumped by makeshift wicket-keeper Gary Kirsten as he charged Nicky Boje and was beaten.

Earlier play was held up for 20 minutes after former skipper and in-form batsman Mohammad Azharuddin was given out caught behind by Kirsten, though the rising ball off Derek Crookes seemed to have hit his left pad.
The decision triggered unrest among spectators who threw water satchels at spinner Paul Adams fielding at square leg, resulting in a walkout by the South Africans, led by Hansie Cronje.
An appeal by Azharuddin calmed the protestors and play resumed after 20 minutes.
Azharuddin's exit and Tendulkar's dismissal caused a slump in the Indian innings, the run rate falling below five runs an over. India scored only 15 runs between the 41st and 45th overs.
But a fierce 54 off 44 balls by Jadeja boosted India's score to a challenging total.
Jadeja's unbeaten knock contained two fours and four sixes, with the last two overs of the Indian innings yielding 34 runs. The worst sufferers were spinners Pat Symcox and Adams.
